page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an ARM-based general-purpose server powered by Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz. It features 2 physical cores assigned to 2 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core. The server includes 8.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Cache architecture consists of 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per socket. It includes hardware AES encryption support, while lacking AVX or AMX instruction extensions. Local storage and discrete GPUs are not bundled with this instance configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate single-threaded CPU throughput alongside limited memory bandwidth. The stress-ng test measured a single-core score of 1812.29 and a multi-core score of 3594.57. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 24.01 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 26.99 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measured 16.42 GB/sec. Complex workloads yield lower relative performance metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1997.0, a PassMark CPU score of 1596.29, and a static web serving throughput of 2.66 GB/sec. Redis SET operations achieved 2.61 million operations per second.

The t2a-standard-2 provides entry-level ARM cloud compute with dedicated vCPU allocation without hyperthreading contention. The hardware profile delivers cost-efficient execution for lightweight ARM-native applications, containerized microservices, basic web serving, and small database workloads. Resource-heavy multi-threaded tasks and large memory bandwidth demands require higher core count instances within the t2a server family.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an ARM-based general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, the server provides 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware AES encryption support. The server contains no local storage or attached GPUs. Benchmark results indicate moderate single-threaded performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1812.29 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 24.01 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics reflect lower relative capacity, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 1997.0 and large block memory write bandwidth of 16.42 GB/sec. The instance delivers steady execution for lightweight scale-out applications, microservices, and entry-level ARM-native web serving.
